fields.event: Underway from Submarine Base, Pearl Harbor, T.H., enroute MIDWAY. Escorted by PC 602 until darkness. Held numerous daily training dives and drills. Fired all guns at a small derelict barge which was a danger to navigation. Sighted several friendly planes.

fields.event: Moored at Submarine Base, MIDWAY. Mooring was subject of special letter forwarded under separate cover. Fueled to capacity.

fields.event: Sighted two ships moored in APRA Harbor. They appeared to be medium freighters and did not appear to be as large as the ships we were chasing. Cut them in and found them to be protected by the reef and OROTE peninsula. Did not deem the chances of hitting were worth the expenditure of torpedoes. If we had been on our way back from station, with torpedoes to spare, would have taken a chance. SHIP CONTACT #3.

fields.event: Leading escort, a CHIDORI, apparently picked us up on his sound gear. Sound conditions unusually good. Convoy zigged away, and port quarter escort, a PC, came over toward us and lay to several hundred yards away, apparently listening. Remained at periscope depth and watched him, as there were several white caps. Saw him signalling to leading escort and finally he resumed his place in the convoy. PC did not echo range, and they apparently only had a doubtful contact. Convoy consisted of 3AK, 1 CHIDORI and 3 PC plus usual air coverage. Convoy was in line of bearing with largest AK in center (a 4500 ton engine aft AK), with two 3000 ton AK in wing positions. Could not obtain favorable firing position. Convoy appeared to be heading toward RABAUL or WEWAK. Trailed at six knots submerged.

fields.event: Experienced radar interference on SJ. This was first noted last night and is mentioned because it seemed to be something new, at least to us.
